name: Amish Friendship Bread
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: Vegetable oil or another neutral-flavored oil
Chopped nuts, such as walnuts or pecans (optional)

steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C, gas mark 4—moderate).
Grease and flour two loaf pans or two 9-inch round cake pans. Alternatively, line them with parchment paper.
Combine the sourdough starter, oil, sugar, and eggs in a large mixing bowl.
Combine the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon in a separate bowl. Stir this dry mixture into the wet mixture.
Stir in the raisins or nuts, if using.
Pour the batter into the prepared pans. Optionally, sprinkle a decorative amount of cinnamon on top of the cake batter.

Bake at 350°F (175°C, gas mark 4—moderate) for about 50–55 minutes if using loaf pans, or about 25–30 minutes if using round cake pans. The cakes are done when a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.

culture.text: Amish friendship bread is a type of bread or cake made from a sourdough starter that is often shared in a manner similar to a chain letter. The starter is a substitute for baking yeast and can be used to make many kinds of yeast-based breads, shared with friends, or frozen for future use. The sweet, cake-like Amish cinnamon bread is a common bread that is made from this starter; it is a simple, stirred quick bread that includes a substantial amount of sugar and vegetable oil, with a mild cinnamon flavor. It has characteristics of both pound cake and coffee cake. The flavor of the finished product can be altered by cinnamon being omitted.
